title: The Picard functor of a proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The *Picard functor*

$$
\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}:(k\text{-algebras})\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab},
\qquad \operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}:=
\bigl(R\longmapsto\operatorname{Pic}(C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}R)\bigr)^{\#}_{\mathrm{fppf}},
$$

is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf of
invertible modules. The fibrewise degree is computed on each residue-field fibre as in [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] and gives the degree morphism [def-pd-degree-morphism]. For
$d\in\mathbf Z$, define $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}:=\deg^{-1}(d)$, the subfunctor
of classes whose degree function is identically $d$ on every base scheme. This
definition fixes the fppf sheafification and its subfunctors
$\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, and nothing else: no
representability of $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$, and no openness
or closedness of the subfunctors $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, is
assumed here.

split_report.summary: The definition is split by naming the existing smooth-projective and geometrically-integral curve notions, relative Picard presheaf, fppf sheafification, fibrewise degree, degree morphism, and inverse-image subfunctor. Pic^d is defined as deg^{-1}(d), namely classes whose degree function is identically d; no representability or openness/closedness is asserted. No new node is needed. The generic Lean definitions picardFunctor and picardFunctorDegree were checked but do not state this item exactly, so they are not attachments.
